predecessors.name: Byzantine Empire
predecessors.text: Crete, conquered 'in either 824 or 827/828' by Andalusian exiles led by Abu Hafs Umar al-Iqritishi

successors.name: Byzantine Empire
successors.text: the whole island, retaken by Nikephoros Phokas: Chandax stormed 6 March 961, 'the rest of Crete quickly capitulated'; it became a Byzantine theme with its strategos at Chandax

ledger.x: 827: Andalusian exiles take Crete and found the emirate.
842: Theoktistos lands an imperial army on Crete.
843: Theoktistos withdraws, the garrison is cut down.
961: the Emirate of Crete falls to Byzantium.

wars.name: Byzantine attempts to retake Crete under Michael II
wars.outcome: Failure: the expedition of Photeinos and Damian was defeated and Damian killed, Krateros' was routed and he was executed; Ooryphas drove the Arabs from the Aegean islands but 'failed to retake Crete'.

wars.name: Theoktistos' expedition to Crete
wars.outcome: Theoktistos 'succeeded in occupying much of the island' but withdrew for political reasons; the troops left behind were slaughtered and the reconquest 'was not completed'.

wars.name: Siege of Chandax (Byzantine reconquest of Crete)
wars.outcome: Byzantine victory: Chandax stormed on 6 March 961, the last emir Abd al-Aziz captured, the island a Byzantine theme.

certainty.note: An island: the coast is the border, but the pages give no survey, the Greek mountain communities were 'left relatively alone', and the Aegean islands that reportedly paid jizya to Crete (Aegina, Elafonisos, Cythera, Naxos, 'could well be…
